AR.name: Carqueja
AR.citation: Steibel, P.E., Nombres y usos de las plantas aplicados por los Indios Ranqueles de La Pampa (Argentina); also documented as Yaguarete-caa. A distinct Ranquel Indigenous name, Kula vodi, is separately recorded for this species by the same source

BO.name: Carqueja
BO.citation: Range confirmed to Andean valleys up to 3000m in Bolivia and Peru, used as stomachic and for liver complaints; also known regionally under Quechua names in Andean tradition

BR.name: Carqueja
BR.citation: Extensive Brazilian academic ethnobotanical and pharmacological literature (Universidade Federal de Ouro Preto; Monteiro et al. 2012 field study in Minas Gerais documenting it as the second most-cited medicinal plant among local herbalists). Core of the species' native range

CL.name: Carqueja
CL.citation: Dieti Natura, listing species-specific distribution including Chile alongside Argentina, Bolivia, Paraguay and Colombia

CO.name: Carqueja
CO.citation: Dieti Natura species-specific distribution list; also referenced at genus level for Colombia in pharmacological literature (PMC6304562)

PE.name: Carqueja
PE.citation: Range confirmed to lower-altitude zones of Peru; used as stomachic and for liver complaints in Andean tradition shared with Bolivia

PY.name: Carqueja
PY.citation: Documented in Paraguayan folk medicine as a blood-sugar regulator, alongside Argentina, motivating preclinical animal research

UY.name: Carqueja
UY.citation: Davies, P. (1995), Malezas comunes y su uso medicinal en el Uruguay, XII Congreso Latinoamericano de Malezas, Facultad de Agronomia, Universidad de la Republica. Documented in Uruguay as a bitter aperitif taken before meals, analogous to gentian or wormwood in European tradition
